newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: APN expects profit improvement for 1997.
newsitem.headline: APN expects profit improvement for 1997.

text.p: Regional media group Australian Provincial Newspapers Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it expects an unspecified improvement in earnings for 1997.
"I can't give an exact projection but we hope for increased profits in 1997," APN chairman Liam Healy told the group's annual meeting.
Healy said the group's regional newspapers division, the biggest in Australia, had started the year reasonably well, while the outdoor advertising business had also begun solidly.
Specialist publishing, which struck difficulties in 1996, was now on track for recovery and an improved performance, Healy said.

The APN annual meeting was prolonged by the appearance of shareholder activist Jack Tilburn, who questioned the board at length on several issues, including corporate governance and the lack of a written a code of ethics for the company.

Under further questioning from Tilburn, Healy said he could not comment on whether APN was a possible bidder for John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, publishers of The Sydney Morning Herald, The Australian Financial Review and Melbourne's The Age newspapers.
"I couldn't comment on that but we'd think about it," he said.
APN is about 49 percent owned by the family interests of Irish businessman Tony O'Reilly and Independent Newspapers Plc, his main media group.
The group reported a 1996 profit of A$26.54 million, up from A$26.39 million the previous year.
